title: The bracketed deployed terminal run returns the reading column unchanged through default -> open -> dismiss
freeze_contract: This file is FROZEN at registration and is never edited again — not to correct a figure, not to widen a claim, not after seeing a result. A prediction that can be amended after the run is a result read backwards. Its CHECKER is a separate file and stays fixable: the checker is logic and will have bugs (the prototype had a real misattribution bug within minutes of being written), while this file is data and its whole value is that it cannot move. If this prediction turns out to be WRONG, that is the finding — record it in the wave Paper and file a NEW prediction with a new id.
claim: Against the deployed build, the round trip runs at all nine swept widths; at every one of the 27 cells (9 reached widths x 3 faces) all six compared fields come back byte-for-byte equal to their pre-open values, at tolerance ZERO; and the absolute figures still match the committed 2026-07-20 default-state table.
this_prediction_can_fail: Three named ways, each readable apart from the others by the `basis` on the field that misses. (1) The round trip does not return the column — before and after disagree in some cell. That is the wave's claim refuted and the whole point of firing the run. (2) A per-face ch constant moves (basis `arithmetic`): the face resolved to a different family, which is instrument/font drift, not a desk fact about dismissal. (3) An absolute px figure moves while before and after still agree (basis `prior-observation`): the desk changed shape since 2026-07-20 — the round trip is still clean and the reading column is still honest, but the registered numbers are stale.

bases.arithmetic: Fixed by the per-face 18px ch math registered in face_constants. A miss is REAL FONT DRIFT — the declared stack resolved to a family other than the forced face.
bases.recomputed: Not read from the artefact at all: the checker DERIVES it from that same row's raw fields. A miss is an internal contradiction in the artefact itself.
bases.ruling: Fixed by a decision rather than by measurement — the instrument's contract, or a charter ruling such as `a fully covered column reports NULL, never FALSE`. A miss means the shipped code no longer matches what was decided.
bases.prior-observation: Read off the committed 2026-07-20 table. A miss is same-build non-determinism or a genuine change in the desk since that run — never, on its own, a round-trip failure.

row_key.note: The composite key, never an index — a sweep reordering would silently compare unrelated cells. It keys on `viewport_px`. It does NOT key on `width`: the round trip's own per-width records name the field `viewport_px`, and tooling written against `r.width` indexes nothing at all and reports a clean empty run.
row_key.inspector_state_note: Every round-trip row is keyed `default`, and that is exact rather than a convenience: BOTH legs the checker compares are default-state readings — the pre-open one and the post-dismiss one. The opened state is the trip, not a measured endpoint.

native.px_per_ch_source: row.ch.probe_px_per_ch — the probe span measured under THIS forced face. The floor-derived ch figure is deliberately not used anywhere in this file: it is unstable per row and carries empty-string values on some rows.
native.ch55_derivation: 55 x 10.0000 px-per-ch, WITHIN THIS FACE ONLY. No figure in this file is ever produced by dividing one face's pixels by another face's ch span.

georgia.px_per_ch_source: row.ch.probe_px_per_ch — the probe span measured under THIS forced face. The floor-derived ch figure is deliberately not used anywhere in this file: it is unstable per row and carries empty-string values on some rows.
georgia.ch55_derivation: 55 x 11.0469 px-per-ch, WITHIN THIS FACE ONLY. No figure in this file is ever produced by dividing one face's pixels by another face's ch span.

source-serif-4.px_per_ch_source: row.ch.probe_px_per_ch — the probe span measured under THIS forced face. The floor-derived ch figure is deliberately not used anywhere in this file: it is unstable per row and carries empty-string values on some rows.
source-serif-4.ch55_derivation: 55 x 9.1719 px-per-ch, WITHIN THIS FACE ONLY. No figure in this file is ever produced by dividing one face's pixels by another face's ch span.

no_cross_face_division: Every ch figure in this file divides one face's own pixels by that same face's own probe span. There is no quotient anywhere whose numerator and denominator come from different faces.

ran.note: A failing open or dismiss leg RETURNS out of the round trip by name, so the run yields either a complete set of cells or none at all. `ran:false` is therefore not a wrong prediction — it is NO EVIDENCE, and the checker reports it as UNEVALUATED with its own exit code. Recording a reachability failure as a refuted fidelity claim would be a lie.

reached_widths.note: the instrument's swept width list, descending

reached_width_count.note: STATED, never assumed. The cell total below is meaningless without it: 27 is a bare number that could describe a partial sweep double-counted, and the reached count is what makes it checkable.

cells_expected_unchanged.derivation: the count of cells whose before[] and after[] agree on all six fields, recomputed by the checker from raw values. The artefact's own summary counters are never read.

compared_fields.note: the instrument's compared-field contract, in order. A different set means a different experiment ran and no cell verdict here is meaningful.

dismiss_control_one_of.note: the two ruled dismissal affordances. A third selector would be an unruled affordance — the trip happened, but not through a grammar anyone decided on.

conditional_rulings.rationale: A fully covered column has no visible width to judge, so the honest report is NULL — absence of a verdict. FALSE would assert the reader was handed a column narrower than the criterion, which is a different and unmeasured claim.
conditional_rulings.applicability_note: This ruling matched ZERO rows of the 2026-07-20 table, so it may well match zero rows of the terminal run too. The checker therefore reports how many rows it applied to and NEVER counts an unexercised ruling as a pass. A guard that reports success from zero applicable rows is the exact defect this whole file exists to refuse.

what_the_checker_may_not_do: The checker RECOMPUTES every verdict from raw values and never reads a row's own verdict field. This is the entire reason the file exists: the wave's existing differ copies the artefact's summary counters straight out of the artefact without recomputing them (studio-desk-compare.mjs:216-218), so it structurally cannot catch a row whose stated verdict contradicts its own raw numbers. Here, a cell claiming it came back unchanged while its own before[] and after[] disagree is caught by name as SELF_INCONSISTENT. The checker also refuses any prediction that leans on the artefact's summary counters at all — on a skipped run those counters read as a clean pass over zero applicable rows, which proves nothing while looking green.
